recentItems.title: How This Interior Designer Maximised Every Awkward Space In His Unconventional One-Bed House
recentItems.description:
A former artist’s studio, Applegarth Studios doesn’t have a single right-angled wall — but the interior designer and owner Nicholas Hodson-Taylor managed to maximise every inch of awkward space with architectural spatial planning and bespoke design. Alongside his husband, the shirtmaker James MacAuslan, he takes us on a tour of this extraordinary London residence to show us how he made the most of the unconventional architecture.

recentItems.title: The Ultimate Guide to Foraged Botanical Displays
recentItems.description:
Welcome to The Art of Style, a brand-new series from The Sunday Times Style. Join artist and writer Rollo Skinner at his home in the Wiltshire / Dorset border as he reveals how to transform the "hedgerow treasures" of the English countryside into a triumphant seasonal display.

In this episode, Rollo breaks down his style philosophy of "simple abundance," showing you how to look beyond the perfect, farmed flowers and find endless magic in the unexpected elements of the landscape: from rusty dock leaves to pendulous sedge. Whether you are creating a party centrepiece or a welcoming display for your entrance hall, learn how to embrace the rhythm of the seasons and bring the beauty of the outdoors in.

What You’ll Learn:
* Slowing Down: Why connecting with nature and observing small details is the essential starting point for all creativity.
* Conditioning: Extend the vase life by conditioning your plants.
* Structure: Master the secret florist’s technique of using chicken wire and water trumpets to create a professional base.
* Refining the Display: Tips on balance, depth, and how to style your surrounding area to turn a simple vase into an immersive world.

Key Materials Featured:
* Earthenware Jug & Chicken Wire
* Foraged Beech & Hornbeam Branches
* Blackberries, Golden Rose Berries & Apples
* Dock Spires, Pendulous Sedge & Sedum

recentItems.title: Inside Tish Weinstock’s Irreverent Countryside Mansion
recentItems.description:
Step inside the wildly eclectic and enchanting Wiltshire countryside home of beauty journalist Tish Weinstock and her husband, Tom Guinness. In this episode of Live with Style, Tish takes us on a fascinating house tour that defies the traditional English country aesthetic, effortlessly blending gothic romanticism with playful maximalism.

Swapping the fast-paced lifestyle of London for the idyllic hills of Wiltshire, Tish has curated a home that proves interior design shouldn’t be taken too seriously. Filled with "idiot tax" vintage finds, optical illusions, and striking art, every room tells a highly personal story. From a dining room wrapped in Iksel trompe l'oeil wallpaper reminiscent of a Napoleonic war tent, to a cozy, Coca-Cola lacquered "Situation Room" library, the house is a masterclass in fearless, rule-breaking design.
Watch as Tish shares the diverse aesthetic inspirations behind her home—ranging from the iconic blue-and-white styling of Colefax and Fowler's Roger Banks-Pye to the monastic Roman bedroom of abstract artist Cy Twombly. Discover her prized 1stDibs vintage Ralph Lauren chair, an iconic Eero Saarinen dining table, and a decidedly daring guest bedroom featuring PVC upholstery and contemporary art by Enrico David and Enzo Cucchi.
Whether you love gothic architecture, high-low design tension, or just want to see how to flawlessly execute a dark-painted room, this countryside estate is endlessly inspiring.
